statement.p: Use polynomial fitting to find the formula for the nth term of the sequence (a_n)_{n \ge 1} which starts,
{3, 5, 9, 15, 23}, \ldots Note the first term above is a_1, not a_0.

solution.p: a_n = {n^{2}-n+3}\text{.} Here we know that we are looking for a quadratic because the second differences are constant. So a_n = an^2 + bn + c\text{.} We can work backwards to find that a_0 = {3}, so we know c= {3}\text{.} Then solve the system,
